sleep_timeout.description: Go to sleep once no buttons have been pressed for this long, while not plugged into USB. Press the wake button to wake back up. Use 0 to never sleep.

syncCalibrations.label: Sync calibrations across inputs
syncCalibrations.description: Syncronise calibrations across inputs that are used multiple times. For example if you have whammy on multiple profiles, turning this on will keep your whammy calibration syncronised, while turning it off means you can have different calibrations per profile.

xinput_on_windows.label: Controller type on Windows (for USB)
xinput_on_windows.description: Pick if you wish to have your controllers emulate an XInput device or an HID device when plugged into a Windows PC. Note that this setting has no effect on macOS, Linux or on game consoles.

ps4EmulationMode.description: Pick the device type to emulate on PS4/5. PS3 works with Rock Band 4 without auth, but won't work in system menus or other games. legendMode.description: Pick the icons to show below. This adjusts the icons and names shown in the UI, such as using A or B instead of Cross and Circle

combinedStrumDebounce.label: Combined strum debounce
combinedStrumDebounce.description: Strum up and down share one debounce window, so a strum is ignored while the other direction is still held or debouncing. Stops a bouncy strum switch registering a strum in the wrong direction. While this is on, changing one strum's debounce changes them all.

queueInputs.label: Queue fret and strum inputs
queueInputs.description: Inputs are read as fast as possible and every fret / strum change is queued, then sent one at a time so the game sees every change, even ones faster than its frame rate. Adds latency while the queue drains.

dequeueInterval.label: Dequeue interval (ms)
dequeueInterval.description: How long each queued state is held for. The game needs to run at {{fps}}+ fps to see every state.

selectToDpadLeft.label: Map Select to D-pad Left on Xbox One/Series and PS4/5
selectToDpadLeft.description: Send Select as D-pad Left instead when plugged into an Xbox One/Series or PS4/5. Rock Band 4 and Fortnite Festival can use D-pad Left to activate star power, which can work better than Select.

ps3OnRpcs3.label: Use USB passthrough with RPCS3
ps3OnRpcs3.description: Switch to PS3 mode when RPCS3 detects the controller, so it can be used with RPCS3's USB passthrough. Turn this off to keep the controller in its PC mode while RPCS3 is running.

fullRangeTurntableOnPc.label: Full range scratching on PC
fullRangeTurntableOnPc.description: Real Xbox 360 turntables only send a tiny range for scratching, which XInput's default deadzone hides on PC. When enabled, scratching uses the full range on PC, and stays accurate to a real turntable when plugged into an Xbox 360.

cymbalGlitchFix.label: Apply the cymbal glitch fix
cymbalGlitchFix.description: Rock band 3 had a bug where hitting two cymbals at the same time would cause one of the cymbals to be dropped. This mitigates that bug, but may not work as well on Rock Band 2. This setting only applies on PS3 and Xbox 360.

assignments.title: Assignments
assignments.description: One of the key improvements with Santroller 2 is that you can have multiple profiles, but this means you need to tell Santroller 2 when you want your profiles used. Assignments are how this is done. Assignments come in two parts - one is the assignment itself, such as say assigning to plugging a Wii Guitar into a Wii Adapter, and the emulation type, such as USB or Bluetooth. This lets you do things like using different profiles for bluetooth vs for USB, but does mean you have to wrap your head around assignments.

direct-pico-guitar.title: Direct-Wired Guitar (Raspberry Pi Pico)
direct-pico-guitar.subtitle: Interactive Wiring & Configuration Walkthrough
direct-pico-guitar.description: Step-by-step interactive build guide for rewiring any Guitar Hero or Rock Band guitar with mechanical or original switches to a Raspberry Pi Pico or Pico 2.

intro.title: 1. Getting Started & Standard Pinout
intro.description: Prepare your tools, microcontroller, and review the standard Santroller wiring plan.
intro.familyGh: Guitar Hero (Les Paul, WT, GH5, Xplorer)
intro.welcome: This guide covers converting or rewiring a Guitar Hero or Rock Band controller to a Raspberry Pi Pico or Pico 2.
intro.directRewireCaption: A direct-wired mechanical switch guitar with a Raspberry Pi Pico
supplies: Raspberry Pi Pico 1 or Pico 2: Any standard RP2040 or RP2350 board.
Soldering iron & solder: 60/40 or lead-free.
Wire (26-30 AWG): Stranded or solid core wire.
Multimeter: Used in continuity mode (the mode that beeps when probes touch) to trace common grounds and signals.
Wire strippers & cutters: For prepping hookup wires.
rules: Find Common Ground: Use a multimeter in continuity mode to identify shared ground traces or wires.
Trace Signal Wires: Trace signal wires for each switch or potentiometer.
Solder & Verify: Solder to your chosen GP pin, then test.
intro.pinoutDesc: Use the default Santroller pin layout or choose your own GPIO pins.

frets.title: 2. Fret Buttons & Slider
frets.description: Connect the 5 fret buttons (Green, Red, Yellow, Blue, Orange) and optional touch slider bar, then verify each input in real time.
frets.intro: The frets are simple mechanical or membrane switches that share a common ground wire and have individual signal wires for each color.
frets.pcbCaption: Example neck PCB showing fret contacts and common ground trace
frets.stepGround: Identify Common Ground: If the neck cable or PCB is not labeled, inspect the neck PCB traces. The trace that loops across all 5 fret switches is your Common Ground.
frets.stepMultimeter: Confirm with Multimeter: In continuity mode, touch one probe to common ground and the other to a fret wire. Pressing that fret should beep.
frets.stepSolderGround: Solder Common Ground: Connect the common ground wire to any GND pin on the Raspberry Pi Pico (e.g., Pin 3 or Pin 8).
frets.stepSolderSignals: Solder Fret Signals: Connect each colored fret signal wire to an unused digital GPIO pin. Our recommended standard uses:
frets.pullUpText: Santroller automatically configures internal pull-up resistors on the Pico for all digital buttons, so you do not need any external resistors. When you press a fret, it shorts the GP pin to Ground.
frets.benchHint: Assign pins manually or click Probe and press the fret button on your guitar to auto-detect its wiring:
frets.gh5Intro: Guitar Hero 5 necks feature a 4-wire digital bus that communicates over I2C. This carries the 5 fret buttons AND the capacitive touch slider bar over just two data pins plus power with zero neck modifications.
frets.gh5PinGnd: GND → Pico Pin 38 (or any GND pin)
frets.gh5VoltageWarning: Always use 3.3V (Pin 36). Never connect the neck to 5V (VBUS); doing so will permanently damage the neck controller IC.
frets.gh5DriverCardDesc: Enable Santroller's built-in GH5 neck driver to automatically configure I2C on GP18/GP19 and map both the frets and the touch slider bar.
frets.gh5DriverActive: I2C Driver Active (GP18 SDA / GP19 SCL)
frets.sliderDesc: The capacitive touch slider bar lets you tap notes in Guitar Hero and Rock Band without strumming. Touch each zone on your physical neck to verify:
frets.rbSoloIntro: Stock Rock Band guitars with solo frets use a 7-wire harness: 5 fret signal lines, 1 upper fret common, and 1 solo fret common. Santroller scans this directly as a 5x2 Matrix across 5 fret signal columns (GP2-GP6) and 2 row outputs (GP14 Upper, GP15 Solo), giving you 10 independent frets with no trace cutting required.
frets.rbSoloMatrixCols: 5 Fret Signal Columns: Green (GP2), Red (GP3), Yellow (GP4), Blue (GP5), Orange (GP6)
frets.rbSoloMatrixUpperRow: Upper Frets Common: GP14 (Pin 19), Matrix Row 1
frets.rbSoloMatrixSoloRow: Solo Frets Common: GP15 (Pin 20), Matrix Row 2
frets.rbSoloMatrixNoGnd: Do not connect the neck common wires to Pico GND. The Pico drives them dynamically as matrix row outputs.
frets.rbSoloDriverDesc: Enable Santroller's built-in Matrix driver to configure GP2-GP6 as column inputs and GP14/GP15 as row outputs, mapping all 10 frets automatically.
frets.rbSoloDriverActive: Matrix Driver Active (GP2-GP6 In / GP14-GP15 Out)
frets.rbShiftedIntro: Some 7-pin Rock Band necks share a common Ground with a dedicated Solo switch line. When a solo fret is pressed, it shorts both that fret's signal and the Solo line to Ground. Santroller models this via Shifted Inputs: normal frets trigger when the fret is pressed without Solo, while solo frets trigger when both are pressed.
frets.rbShiftedDriverDesc: Configure all 10 frets automatically using Shifted inputs on GP2-GP6 with GP12 as the Solo modifier.
frets.rbSplitIntro: If you have run dedicated wires from the lower neck PCB to the main body, each solo fret has its own distinct GPIO pin, allowing 10 simultaneous inputs without multiplexing.
frets.mpr121Intro: Guitar Hero World Tour guitars used a single-wire analog slider bar with high latency and limited chord detection. Bypassing the stock chip with an MPR121 capacitive touch breakout over I2C provides ultra-low latency multi-touch tracking.
frets.mpr121StepTraces: Cut traces leading away from chip U2 (or desolder U2 entirely) on the slider PCB as shown in the diagram.
frets.mpr121TracesCaption: Trace cuts around U2 on the World Tour slider PCB
frets.mpr121StepVias: Solder wires from each via (channels 0 through 4) on the slider PCB to channels 0-4 on the MPR121 breakout.
frets.mpr121ViasCaption: Slider via locations to solder to MPR121 channels 0-4
frets.mpr121StepFrets: Connect the 5 fret signal wires to MPR121 channels 5-9, or wire them directly to Pico GPIOs GP2-GP6.
frets.mpr121StepI2c: Connect the MPR121 to the Pico over I2C: 3.3V (Pin 36), GND (Pin 38), SDA (GP18 / Pin 24), and SCL (GP19 / Pin 25).

strum.title: 3. Strum Bar Switches
strum.description: Connect Strum Up and Strum Down switches, cut board traces if reusing original PCBs, and test switch actuation.
strum.intro: The strum bar is operated by two switches: Strum Up and Strum Down. Like the frets, these two switches share a common ground wire.
strum.strumPcbCaption: Strum switches on an original main PCB
strum.directIntro: When using replacement mechanical switches (like Kailh Box switches) or a 3D-printed strum bracket, the switches are completely isolated from stock circuitry.
strum.directStepGround: Common Ground: Connect one pin of each switch together and wire to any GND pin on the Pico.
strum.directStepUp: Strum Up: Connect the signal contact to GP7 (Pin 10).
strum.directStepDown: Strum Down: Connect the signal contact to GP8 (Pin 11).
strum.cutTraceDesc1: If your strum switches are soldered directly to an original console PCB (such as Wii, Xbox 360, or PS3), they remain connected to the original console microcontroller and capacitors. This causes phantom or stuck inputs unless traces are cut.
strum.cutTraceDesc2: Use a craft knife or razor to score and sever the copper traces leading away from the switch pins. Use your multimeter in continuity mode to confirm each switch contact is isolated from the rest of the board.
strum.cutTraceCaption: Cutting copper traces around strum switch contacts
strum.benchHint: Assign pins manually or flick the strum bar to auto-detect the switch:
strum.debounceDesc: Mechanical strum switches can bounce on release, causing unwanted double strums. You can fine-tune Strum Debounce in Profile Poll Settings if you notice accidental over-strums.

whammy.title: 4. Whammy Bar Potentiometer
whammy.description: Wire the 10k potentiometer to 3.3V, Ground, and ADC0 (GP26), then test live analog movement.
whammy.intro: The whammy bar connects to an analog potentiometer (typically 10kΩ). Unlike digital buttons which are on or off, the whammy measures variable depth and must connect to one of the Pico's dedicated Analog ADC pins.
whammy.potCenter: Center Pin (Signal / Wiper): Solder to GP26 (ADC0 / Pin 31) on your Pico.
whammy.potOuter1: Outer Pin 1: Solder to 3V3(OUT) (Pin 36) on your Pico.
whammy.potOuter2: Outer Pin 2: Solder to GND (Pin 38) on your Pico.
whammy.invertNote: (Note: If the whammy value decreases when pressed instead of increasing, you can either swap the two outer wires or toggle "Invert" in calibration.)
whammy.warning2WireDesc: Some stock guitars have a potentiometer PCB where two pins are bridged, leaving only 2 wires exposed. You must desolder the bridged connection and solder 3 distinct wires directly to the 3 potentiometer pins.
whammy.warning2WireCaption: Desoldering bridged pins to wire 3 full lines (3V3, Signal, GND)
whammy.pickupIntro: Rock Band Stratocaster and Precision Bass guitars include a 5-way pickup selector switch for guitar effects. Like the whammy, it connects to an analog ADC pin (GP27 / ADC1).
whammy.pickupCenter: Signal / Wiper Pin: Connect to GP27 (ADC1 / Pin 32).
whammy.pickup2WireDesc: On the Rock Band Precision Bass, the pickup potentiometer PCB bridges two pins. Desolder the small attached PCB and run 3 distinct wires directly from the potentiometer pins to 3.3V, GP27, and GND.
whammy.benchHint: Verify analog ADC input. Move the whammy bar to watch the live progress bar respond:
whammy.verificationDesc: When wired correctly, releasing the whammy should show a steady low or high value, and pressing the whammy bar will smoothly increase or decrease the reading.

tilt.title: 5. Star Power Tilt Sensor
tilt.description: Connect a ball tilt switch to GP11 or an I2C accelerometer to trigger Star Power / Overdrive.
tilt.intro: Tilt sensors activate Star Power / Overdrive when you tilt the guitar neck upward. Santroller supports digital ball tilt switches and I2C accelerometers.
tilt.digitalIntro: A ball tilt switch (such as the SW-520D) opens or closes when tilted at roughly 45°.
tilt.seriesTipTitle: Tip: Wire two switches in series
tilt.seriesTipDesc: To prevent false triggers from hard strumming, wire two tilt switches in series. Both switches must close simultaneously to trigger Star Power.
tilt.digitalPinGnd: Connect one pin of the tilt sensor to any GND on the Pico.
tilt.digitalPinGp: Connect the other pin to GP11 (Pin 15).
tilt.digitalMount: Mount the sensor inside the guitar body angled slightly upward towards the neck.
tilt.i2cIntro: Accelerometers measure gravitational acceleration along 3 axes for tilt detection.
tilt.benchHint: Tilt the guitar body upward to test activation:
tilt.invertDesc: If your tilt sensor triggers when resting and turns off when lifted, toggle "Invert" in the input settings.

nav.title: 6. Start, Select & Menu Navigation
nav.description: Wire the Start and Select buttons to GP9 and GP10, and optionally configure the Home combo.
nav.intro: Start (Pause / Plus) and Select (Star Power / Minus) buttons let you navigate menus and pause songs.
nav.navGround: Find Common Ground: Follow the traces between the Start and Select contacts or use continuity mode on your multimeter. Connect the common ground to any GND pin on the Pico.
nav.startSignal: Start Button Signal: Connect the Start signal wire to GP9 (Pin 12).
nav.selectSignal: Select Button Signal: Connect the Select signal wire to GP10 (Pin 14).
nav.comboDesc: You can configure a shortcut in Santroller to map Start + Select to the Guide / Home button if your guitar lacks a dedicated guide button.
nav.benchHint: Assign pins or click Probe and press Start or Select to test:

review.title: 7. Complete & Final Verification
review.description: Verify all guitar inputs and save your configuration to the Pico.
review.buildCompleteDesc: All inputs have been wired and mapped.
review.finalVerificationDesc: Use the diagnostic panel on the right to test every switch, strum, and the whammy bar. Press chord combinations and flick the strum bar up and down rapidly to ensure clean actuation.
review.saveDesc: When all inputs test correctly, click Save Configuration to Pico to write your settings to flash memory.
review.savedSuccessDesc: Configuration saved to Pico flash memory.

wii-adapter.description: Build an adapter using a Raspberry Pi Pico to use any Wii Guitar Hero or Rock Band guitar on PC or console with zero soldering to the guitar itself.

wii-intro.title: 1. Supplies & Overview
wii-intro.description: Learn the 4-wire I2C pinout needed to adapt any Wii controller to USB.
wii-intro.intro: The Wii Guitar Adapter lets you plug any original Nintendo Wii guitar (Les Paul, World Tour, GH5) or Classic Controller into a Raspberry Pi Pico and use it on PC or consoles with ultra-low latency.

wii-intro.quickStartDesc: Wii controllers communicate over I2C. Connect 4 wires between the Wii connector and Pico:

wii-wiring.description: Wire 3.3V, Ground, SDA, and SCL, and enable the Wii Extension driver in Santroller.
wii-wiring.intro: Connect the 4 wires from your Wii female connector or breakout board to the Raspberry Pi Pico.
wii-wiring.voltageWarningText: Wii controllers operate strictly at 3.3V. Connect VCC to the Pico's 3V3(OUT) (Pin 36), never to VBUS (5V).
wii-wiring.wireColorWarningText: Third-party extension cables often use arbitrary wire colors. Verify each pin with a multimeter using the pinout diagram above.

wii-test.btnSave: Save Adapter Configuration to Pico Flash

ps2-adapter.title: PS2 Controller & Guitar to USB Adapter
ps2-adapter.subtitle: SPI Bus Adapter for DualShock 2 & PS2 Guitars
ps2-adapter.description: Convert any original Sony PlayStation 1 or 2 gamepad, arcade stick, or Guitar Hero guitar to USB using a Raspberry Pi Pico.

ps2-intro.title: 1. PS2 Socket Pinout & Supplies
ps2-intro.description: Overview of the PS2 controller SPI protocol and required 1kΩ pull-up resistors.
ps2-intro.intro: Build a high-polling PS2 controller adapter for PlayStation 1 and PlayStation 2 controllers, including DualShock, DualShock 2, and PS2 Guitar Hero / Rock Band guitars.
supplies: Raspberry Pi Pico 1 or Pico 2
PS2 Controller Socket or cut extension cable
2x 1kΩ Resistors (used as pull-up resistors for MISO and Acknowledge lines)
Soldering Iron & Wire
ps2-intro.logicLevelWarningText: PlayStation 2 controllers are designed to run at 3.3V. Always connect the controller power line to the Pico's 3V3(OUT) (Pin 36), never to VBUS (5V), to prevent long-term damage.
ps2-intro.pinoutSummaryDesc: Standard Santroller pin layout for PS2 controllers (SPI Channel 0):

ps2-wiring.title: 2. Solder Wires & Enable Driver
ps2-wiring.description: Connect the 6 signal and power wires and enable the PS2 controller driver.
solderingSteps: Solder Clock (SCK): Connect PS2 Pin 5 to GP6 (Pin 9).
Solder Command (MOSI): Connect PS2 Pin 2 to GP3 (Pin 5).
Solder Data (MISO) & Resistor: Connect PS2 Pin 1 to GP4 (Pin 6). Place a 1kΩ resistor between GP4 and 3V3 (Pin 36).
Solder Acknowledge & Resistor: Connect PS2 Pin 9 to GP7 (Pin 10). Place a 1kΩ resistor between GP7 and 3V3 (Pin 36).
Solder Attention (ATT): Connect PS2 Pin 6 to GP10 (Pin 14).
Power & Ground: Connect PS2 Pin 4 to 3V3(OUT) (Pin 36) and PS2 Pin 7 to GND (Pin 38).
ps2-wiring.driverStatusDesc: Enable the PlayStation 2 controller hardware driver in Santroller:

drum-intro.title: 1. Supplies & Drum Architecture
drum-intro.description: Understanding piezo velocity sensors, protection diodes, and multiplexer expansion.
drum-intro.intro: Build a custom drum kit or convert existing Guitar Hero / Rock Band drum pads using a Raspberry Pi Pico. Santroller supports both direct piezo triggers with velocity sensing and analog multiplexers (74HC4051 / 74HC4067).
supplies: Raspberry Pi Pico 1 or Pico 2
Piezo Electric Sensors (1 per drum pad / cymbal)
1MΩ Resistors (1 per piezo to pull signal to ground)
3.3V Zener Diodes (to protect microcontroller inputs from high voltage spikes)
74HC4051 or 74HC4067 Multiplexer: Required if using more than 3-4 analog pads on a standard Pico.
drum-intro.layoutDesc: Official Rock Band and Guitar Hero color arrangement:

drum-wiring.title: 2. Piezo Wiring & Velocity Calibration
drum-wiring.description: Connect piezo discs with 1MΩ resistors and 3.3V zener diodes, then test strike velocity.
drum-wiring.intro: Piezos generate an analog voltage pulse proportional to how hard you hit the drum pad.
drum-wiring.polarityWarningText: Piezo discs are directional. Connect the outer brass ring (black wire) to Ground and the inner ceramic disc (red wire) to the Analog Input. If hits register weakly, swap the wires.
wiringSteps: Solder Black Wire to Ground: Connect the outer brass ring (black wire) to a common GND.
Solder Red Wire to Analog Pin: Connect the inner ceramic disc (red wire) to an ADC pin (GP26, GP27, GP28) or multiplexer channel.
1MΩ Resistor: Connect a 1MΩ resistor between the signal line and ground to pull the line low when not hit.
3.3V Zener Diode: Connect a 3.3V zener diode between signal and ground (cathode to signal, anode to ground) to clamp spikes over 3.3V.
drum-wiring.hitMonitorDesc: Tap the pads to verify velocity response:

drum-test.description: Perform strike tests across all pads and cymbals, then save to Pico flash.
drum-test.calibratedText: Drum trigger inputs and thresholds are saved and ready for use.
drum-test.tipsText: If hitting one drum triggers an adjacent drum (cross-talk), you can increase the threshold or adjust debounce settings under Profile Poll Settings.

dj-turntable.description: Rewire any DJ Hero turntable to a Raspberry Pi Pico for low-latency scratch vinyl and crossfader controls in DJ Hero.

tt-intro.title: 1. Supplies & Pinout Plan
tt-intro.description: Understand the turntable platter optical sensor, crossfader pot, and face buttons.
tt-intro.intro: Convert an original DJ Hero Turntable controller (Xbox 360, PS3, or Wii) into a low-latency USB scratch controller for DJ Hero.
supplies: Raspberry Pi Pico 1 or Pico 2
DJ Hero Turntable Controller
Soldering Iron & Wire
tt-intro.subsystemsIntro: A complete DJ Hero turntable consists of four distinct sections:
subsystems: Spinning Platter: High-resolution optical encoder reporting scratch direction and speed.
Platter Buttons: 3 buttons on the vinyl disc (Green, Red, Blue).
Crossfader: Center-notched 10k potentiometer with Left / Center / Right zones.
Effects Dial & Euphoria: Rotary potentiometer and glowing Euphoria button.
tt-intro.pinoutDesc: Recommended Raspberry Pi Pico pin connections:

tt-wiring.title: 2. Platter & Crossfader Wiring
tt-wiring.description: Wire the optical encoder, platter buttons, crossfader, and effects dial.
wiringSteps: Platter Encoder (I2C): Locate the platter connector pads labelled V, G, C, and D. Connect V to 3V3(OUT), G to GND, C to GP19 (SCL), and D to GP18 (SDA).
Crossfader Potentiometer: Connect outer pins to 3V3 and GND; connect the center wiper pin to GP26 (ADC0).
Effects Dial: Connect outer pins to 3V3 and GND; connect the wiper pin to GP27 (ADC1).
Platter Buttons: Follow the traces from the 3 platter button contacts. Solder the common line to GND, and connect the Green, Red, and Blue lines to GP2, GP3, and GP4.

tt-test.title: 3. Live Test & Save
tt-test.description: Verify scratch rotation, crossfader calibration, and save turntable firmware.
tt-test.configuredText: Turntable inputs are calibrated and ready for use.
tt-test.scratchTestText: Spin the platter forward and backward. The optical sensor should cleanly register rotation ticks in both directions without skipping. Slide the crossfader left and right to verify full travel.
tt-test.btnSave: Save Turntable Configuration to Pico Flash
tt-test.verifyPrompt: Spin the turntable to test live scratching.

Soldering Iron & Wire
usb-intro.pinoutTitle: USB Pinout on Raspberry Pi Pico

usb-wiring.title: 2. Solder D+/D- and Enable Driver
usb-wiring.description: Connect the 4 USB wires and activate the USB Host driver in Santroller.
wiringSteps: Power (Red): Solder the Red wire to VBUS (Pin 40). This provides 5V to the connected USB controller.
Ground (Black): Solder the Black wire to any GND (Pin 38).
D+ (Green): Solder the Green wire to an unused digital GPIO, such as GP2 (Pin 4).
D- (White): Solder the White wire to the pin immediately adjacent to D+, which is GP3 (Pin 5).

rgb-leds.description: Add addressable RGB LEDs to your guitar or drum kit that light up on button presses and sync with Star Power in games like YARG.

led-intro.title: 1. Supplies & LED Wiring Scheme
led-intro.description: Overview of addressable RGB LEDs, power distribution, and protection resistors.
led-intro.intro: Add RGB LEDs or addressable LED strips (APA102, SK9822, WS2812B) to your controller. Supports reactive lighting on button presses, idle animations, and game integrations.
led-intro.inlineCaption: RGB LEDs installed behind guitar fret buttons
supplies: Raspberry Pi Pico 1 or Pico 2
Addressable RGB LEDs (APA102 / SK9822 DotStar or WS2812B NeoPixels)
330Ω to 470Ω Resistor (in series on the data line to prevent voltage spikes)
1000µF Capacitor (across 5V power and ground to smooth out sudden current draws)
Soldering Iron & Wire

led-wiring.title: 2. Solder LEDs & Data Line
led-wiring.description: Connect power from VBUS, chain LEDs in series, and add inline protection.
wiringSteps: 5V Power: Connect the 5V line of your LED strip or fret LEDs to VBUS (Pin 40) on the Pico.
Ground: Connect the ground line to any GND (Pin 38).
Data Line: Solder a 330Ω to 470Ω resistor inline between GP3 (Pin 5) and the Data In (DI) pin of the first LED.
Chaining LEDs: Connect the Data Out (DO) of the first LED to the Data In (DI) of the next, until all LEDs are connected in series.

led-test.title: 3. Live Test & Save
led-test.description: Test fret animations, configure idle timer, and save LED configuration to flash.
led-test.configuredText: LED hardware and lighting modes are configured.
led-test.syncText: Santroller includes an automatic inactivity timer that shuts LEDs off after a period of non-use. You can also link any LED to game events (like Star Power or combo streaks) in YARG.
led-test.btnSave: Save LED Configuration to Pico Flash
led-test.verifyPrompt: Press fret buttons to verify real-time LED triggering.

supportedHardware.title: Supported Hardware
supportedHardware.subtitle: Microcontrollers, USB devices, sensors and accessories that work with Santroller.
supportedHardware.alertBody: Santroller runs on a Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040 or RP2350). You can wire buttons, switches and LEDs straight to the GPIO pins, read Wii and PS2 controllers over their original connectors, or use the USB Host port for controllers, wireless dongles and auth devices.
supportedHardware.cloneWarningTitle: Watch out for fake "Pico W" boards
supportedHardware.cloneWarningBody: A lot of cheap "Pico W" boards on AliExpress and similar sites swap the CYW43439 wireless chip for an ESP8266 or ESP8285. Those chips are Wi-Fi only and have no Bluetooth, so they won't work with any Santroller Bluetooth features, including wireless controllers and Wii Remote emulation. A genuine Pico W / Pico 2 W has a silver metal shield over the wireless chip with the Raspberry Pi logo on it.

pico_rp2040.description: The standard Raspberry Pi Pico. Polls inputs in under a millisecond and has 26 usable GPIO pins.

3 ADC pins for whammy, analog sticks or piezos
PIO is used for the USB host port and console controller protocols

pico2_rp2350.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350)

Uses the Santroller Pico 2 firmware build

pico_w_wireless.name: Raspberry Pi Pico W / Pico 2 W

Can be used as a low-latency Bluetooth transmitter inside a wireless guitar
Pairs with a second Pico acting as the receiver
Can run off a battery on VSYS, with a Schottky diode for reverse protection
pico_w_wireless.warning: Some cheap AliExpress "Pico W" boards use an ESP8285 / ESP8266 instead of the CYW43439. Those are Wi-Fi only, have no Bluetooth, and won't work. Genuine boards have a silver metal shield over the wireless chip marked "Raspberry Pi".

periph_crkd_neck.description: Reads CRKD guitar necks, which use a PY32F002B microcontroller.
details: 460.8 kbps serial with CRC-8 checking
Frets, solo frets and the neck D-pad
Supports the neck's WS2812 LEDs

periph_protar_neck.name: Mad Catz Rock Band 3 Pro Guitar Neck
periph_protar_neck.description: Reads the 102-button Rock Band 3 Mustang and Squier Pro Guitar necks.
details: All 17 frets on all 6 strings (102 switches)
Frets, solo flags and navigation buttons
Uses MOSI, MISO, SCK and Attention / Chip Select

periph_crazy_guitar.name: Crazy Guitar / RedOctane Custom Neck
periph_crazy_guitar.description: Reads Crazy Guitar neck boards over I2C.
details: 5 frets, read from the neck's microcontroller
Works with both 3.3V and 5V necks

periph_wt_drum.name: Guitar Hero World Tour Drum Module
periph_wt_drum.description: Reads the drum module inside Guitar Hero World Tour drum kits.
details: Hits and velocity for the 3 pads, 2 cymbals and kick pedal
Uses SPI with its own Chip Select line

periph_bh_drum.name: Band Hero / Guitar Hero 5 Drum Module
periph_bh_drum.description: Reads the drum module in Band Hero and GH5 drum kits.
details: Pad and cymbal velocity over I2C
Keeps the stock drum electronics and piezos

periph_crkd_drum.name: CRKD Electronic Drum Interface
periph_crkd_drum.description: Reads CRKD drum kit modules over serial.
details: Direct serial connection
Pads, cymbals and kick pedal

periph_djh_turntable.name: DJ Hero Turntable Platter Sub-Module
periph_djh_turntable.description: Reads the platter module from a DJ Hero turntable.
details: Platter rotation and the 3 stream buttons (Green / Red / Blue)
Left or right hand orientation, polled every 5 ms

periph_infinium_fader.name: Infinium Optical Contactless Crossfader
periph_infinium_fader.description: Optical crossfader used in DJ mixers and custom scratch builds.
details: Optical, so it doesn't wear out like a pot
Read over serial

periph_vtech_guitar.name: VTech KidiStar Guitar I/O Expander
periph_vtech_guitar.description: Reads the VTech KidiStar guitar's I/O expander, so it can be converted into a Santroller controller.
details: SPI with an attention line
Reads its button and fret matrix

periph_secondary_pico.name: Secondary Pi Pico (I2C Coprocessor)
periph_secondary_pico.description: Put a second Pico in the guitar neck to read the frets and sensors there, and send them to the main Pico over I2C.
details: The second Pico runs the Santroller peripheral firmware
Only 4 wires between body and neck (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL)
Can handle buttons, matrices or LEDs in the neck

exp_mpr121.name: MPR121 Capacitive Touch & Slider Sensor
exp_mpr121.description: 12-channel capacitive touch sensor. The best way to rewire a Guitar Hero World Tour touch slider.
details: 12 touch channels with automatic calibration
Channels 0-4 are the slider segments, and the rest can be used for frets
Much faster and more reliable than the stock World Tour slider

exp_multiplexer.name: Analog / Digital Multiplexers (CD4051 & CD4067)
exp_multiplexer.description: Turn one GPIO or analog pin into 8 or 16 inputs with a CD74HC4051 (8 channels) or CD74HC4067 (16 channels).
details: CD4051: 8 channels, 3 address pins (S0-S2) and 1 signal pin
CD4067: 16 channels, 4 address pins (S0-S3) and 1 signal pin
Works for both analog inputs and buttons
Scanning is handled by the firmware

exp_matrix_switch_network.name: Key Matrix & Switch Networks (Dioded)
exp_matrix_switch_network.description: Read lots of buttons with only a few pins, using a diode matrix or a resistor network.
details: Matrices of up to 32 pins, with diodes to prevent ghosting
Switch network support for resistor-based button networks
Useful for arcade panels, dance pads and keyboards

exp_ads1115.name: ADS1115 16-Bit Precision ADC
exp_ads1115.description: 16-bit ADC for whammy, analog sticks or piezos when you need more resolution than the Pico's built-in ADC.
details: 4 single-ended or 2 differential channels
Programmable gain and an alert/interrupt pin
Less noise and more resolution than the Pico's 12-bit ADC

exp_rotary_encoder.name: Hardware Quadrature Rotary Encoders
exp_rotary_encoder.description: Optical and mechanical rotary encoders, for DJ Hero platters, dials and spinners.
details: Read with PIO so ticks aren't missed at high speed
Direction detection and adjustable sensitivity

led_addressable_rgb.name: Addressable RGB LEDs (WS2812B / Neopixels)
led_addressable_rgb.description: Addressable LED strips and individual LEDs, driven by PIO.
details: WS2812B, SK6812 (RGBW) and WS2813
Frets light up in their note color when pressed
Lighting for strums and Star Power / Overdrive
Player number and idle animations

led_apa102.name: APA102 / DotStar High-Speed SPI LEDs
led_apa102.description: Addressable LEDs with a separate clock line, so they don't have the timing issues of single-wire LEDs.
details: Hardware SPI at up to 12 MHz
Separate data (MOSI) and clock (SCK) lines
RGB or BGR color order

led_stp16cpc.name: STP16CPC26 Constant-Current LED Driver
led_stp16cpc.description: 16-channel constant-current LED driver, for original guitar LEDs, button backlights or arcade buttons.
details: 16 outputs, with one resistor setting the current for all of them
Controlled over SPI (MOSI, SCK, LE, OE)
No resistor needed per LED, which suits custom PCBs and lit frets

led_dmx512.name: DMX512 Stage Lighting Interface
led_dmx512.description: Drive DMX stage lights, strobes and smoke machines in time with the game.
details: Outputs DMX512 at 250 kbps over RS-485
Lights can react to notes, streaks, Star Power and game state

led_discrete.name: Discrete Single-Color LEDs
led_discrete.description: Ordinary single-color LEDs, such as the original faceplate LEDs or player lights, each with a resistor.
details: Player 1-4 lights
Star Power / Overdrive indicator
Low battery warning (Pico W wireless builds)

pwr_max1704x.name: MAX17043 / MAX17048 Fuel Gauge IC
pwr_max1704x.description: Battery fuel gauge for LiPo / Li-ion cells, giving an accurate charge percentage.
details: Reports battery voltage and percentage over I2C
Alert pin for low battery
Battery level is reported to the console (PS3, PS4, Switch, Wii)

pwr_adc_battery.name: ADC Voltage Divider Battery Monitor
pwr_adc_battery.description: Measure a single-cell LiPo using the Pico's built-in 3:1 voltage divider.
details: GP29 reads VSYS (about 3.3V empty to 4.2V full)
Divider ratio and voltage thresholds can be set in the Configurator
Shows low battery on the console and can trigger sleep, no extra parts needed

pwr_management_sleep.name: Power Management & Inactivity Sleep
pwr_management_sleep.description: Turn off LEDs and other hardware when the controller isn't being used.
details: Heartbeat pin to stop power banks from turning off
Inactivity pin can switch a MOSFET to cut power and save battery
Wakes up on any fret, strum or button press

bus_wii_extension.name: Wii Extension Bus (I2C Input)
bus_wii_extension.description: Read Wii Guitar Hero guitars, drums or Nunchuks through the Wii extension connector.
details: Plug the controller in as-is, no need to open it up
Frets, strum, whammy, joystick and touch slider
Makes a USB adapter for Wii instruments

bus_wii_emulation.name: Wii Extension Port Emulation (Hardware Bus)
bus_wii_emulation.description: Act as a Wii extension (Guitar Hero guitar or Classic Controller) so you can plug into a real Wii Remote.
details: Santroller handles the encrypted extension protocol
Plug into a Wii Remote to play Wii Guitar Hero wirelessly

bus_ps2_controller.name: PlayStation 1 & 2 Controller Bus (SPI Input)
bus_ps2_controller.description: Read PS1 / PS2 controllers and Guitar Hero SG guitars.
details: PS2 Guitar Hero SG guitars and DualShock 2 controllers
Pressure-sensitive buttons and analog sticks
Makes a USB adapter for PS2 instruments

bus_ps2_emulation.name: PlayStation 1 & 2 Port Emulation (Output)
bus_ps2_emulation.interfaceType: SPI pins (CMD, ATT, ACK, DATA, CLK)
bus_ps2_emulation.description: Act as a PS1 / PS2 controller so you can plug into a real PlayStation or PS2.
details: Can act as a DualShock or Guitar Hero SG guitar
Plugs straight into the console's controller port

bus_snes_pad.name: Super Nintendo (SNES) / NES Controller Bus
details: Standard 4021 shift register controllers over clock, latch and data
Read in under a millisecond

bus_joybus.name: Nintendo Joybus (N64 & GameCube Controller Bus)
details: Joybus protocol handled with PIO
GameCube controllers, DK Bongos and N64 controllers

bus_joybus_emulation.name: GameCube / Joybus Port Emulation (Output)
bus_joybus_emulation.description: Act as a GameCube controller, for GameCube consoles and the Wii's GameCube ports.
details: Works with GameCube, the Wii's GameCube ports, and GameCube USB adapters
Joybus timing handled with PIO

bus_xbox360_rf.name: Xbox 360 RF Wireless Module (Front Panel)
bus_xbox360_rf.description: Wire up the front-panel RF board from an Xbox 360 to make a wireless receiver.
details: Works with RF boards from both original and Slim consoles
Wireless controllers, guitars and drums
The SYNC button and Ring of Light LEDs work

bus_midi.name: MIDI 5-Pin DIN & USB-MIDI Devices
bus_midi.description: Connect electronic drum kits, MIDI keyboards or other MIDI devices.
details: 5-pin DIN MIDI IN using an optocoupler on a UART (31,250 baud)
USB MIDI devices on the USB Host port
Bluetooth MIDI for wireless drum kits
Map MIDI notes and velocity to Rock Band Pro Drums pads and cymbals

compatibility.title: Console Compatibility
compatibility.subtitle: Which emulation mode to use on each console, how console authentication works, and setup for Wii Brainslug and PS2 PADEMU.

pc.games: Clone Hero, YARG, Fortnite Festival, emulators (RPCS3, PCSX2, Dolphin)
pc.recommendedMode: XInput or DirectInput (Gamepad / GH Guitar / RB Guitar)
pc.notes: No setup needed. Whammy, tilt and RGB LEDs all work.

ps3.games: Guitar Hero, Rock Band, DJ Hero and regular games
ps3.recommendedMode: PS3 Guitar / PS3 Drums / PS3 Gamepad
ps3.notes: Works out of the box. The PS3 doesn't authenticate controllers.

ps2_usb.games: Rock Band 1 & 2, GH World Tour, GH5, Band Hero
ps2_usb.recommendedMode: Rock Band Guitar / Drums or GH Guitar
ps2_usb.notes: These later PS2 rhythm games support USB instruments directly.

ps2_pademu.recommendedMode: PS3 Gamepad / Guitar (with PADEMU) or PS2 controller bus
ps2_pademu.connection: USB (with PADEMU) or PS2 controller port
ps2_pademu.notes: Older PS2 games only read controllers in the front controller ports. Either use OPL with PADEMU, or wire the Pico to a PS2 controller port.

ps4_rb4.notes: Rock Band 4 accepts PS3 instruments without authentication, but you can't use them to navigate the PS4 home menu.

ps4_native.games: PS4 games, including the home menu
ps4_native.notes: Needs authentication. Plug a DualShock 4 or Mayflash MAGPS4 into the Santroller USB Host port.

ps45_festival.notes: Use a Keyboard profile. Keyboards don't need to authenticate, and you can bind whatever keys you like.

ps5_rb4.notes: Rock Band 4 accepts PS3 instruments without authentication.

ps5_native.notes: PS5 games need a Besavior P5General plugged into the Santroller USB Host port.

x360.games: Guitar Hero, Rock Band, DJ Hero and regular games
x360.notes: Santroller handles Xbox 360 authentication itself, so no extra hardware is needed.

xbone_festival.notes: Use a Keyboard profile. Keyboards don't need to authenticate, and you can bind whatever keys you like.

xbone_native.games: Rock Band 4 and other Xbox One / Series games
xbone_native.connection: USB Host passthrough or I2C auth chip
xbone_native.notes: Authenticate with an official or most third-party Xbox One controllers on the USB Host port, or with an auth chip taken from an Xbox One controller and wired over I2C.
xbone_native.pluginOrAuth: <auth>Xbox One controller or I2C auth chip</auth>

wii_rb.notes: Wii Rock Band games use USB instruments. Set the emulation mode to Rock Band and plug in.

wii_gh.games: Guitar Hero, Band Hero, DJ Hero
wii_gh.recommendedMode: Wii Remote emulation (Pico W or Bluetooth dongle)
wii_gh.connection: Bluetooth, USB (Brainslug) or Wii extension cable
wii_gh.notes: Santroller can act as a Wii Remote over Bluetooth using a Pico W or a USB Bluetooth dongle. This works on an unmodified Wii with retail discs. Otherwise, use Brainslug on a modded Wii or wire up a Wii extension cable.

switch.games: All Switch games (e.g. Taiko, Rhythm Sprout)
switch.notes: Enable "Pro Controller Wired Communication" under System Settings → Controllers and Sensors.

ogxbox.notes: Santroller speaks the original Xbox controller protocol. You need a USB to Xbox controller port adapter cable.

modes.intro: Set the emulation mode under Controller Settings → Emulation Type.

ghGuitar.title: Guitar Hero Guitar
ghGuitar.description: Acts like a Guitar Hero guitar on PS3, Xbox 360, Wii and PS2: five frets, strum up/down, whammy, tilt and Star Power.
features: Works with Guitar Hero games on PS3, 360 and Wii
Supports the touch slider on guitars that have one

rbGuitar.title: Rock Band Guitar
rbGuitar.description: Acts like a Rock Band Stratocaster: five frets plus five solo frets, the 5-way pickup switch, whammy and tilt for Overdrive.
features: Solo frets register as solo notes in Rock Band
Pickup switch controls the effects in RB2, RB3 and RB4
Works over USB in Rock Band 1 to 4

rbDrums.title: Rock Band Drums & Pro Drums
rbDrums.description: Four pads, kick pedal and optional Pro Drums cymbals, with velocity.
features: Pro Drums cymbals are reported separately to Rock Band 3 and 4
Electronic drum kits work over MIDI IN or USB MIDI
Crosstalk and debounce filtering for piezo pads

djh.title: DJ Hero Turntable
djh.description: Acts like a DJ Hero turntable: platter encoders, the three stream buttons, crossfader, Euphoria button and effects dial.

festival.title: Fortnite Festival
festival.description: Fortnite Festival is set up with a profile rather than a dedicated mode, so you choose the key bindings yourself.
features: Key bindings: Pick the key for every fret, strum direction and menu button.
Presets: Load bindings for Lead Guitar, Pro Guitar, Drums or Pro Drums in one click.
Consoles: A Keyboard profile works on PS4, PS5 and Xbox without authentication.
Overdrive: Turn on 'Select to D-pad Left' in the profile options so Select triggers Overdrive.

gamepad.title: Gamepad & Arcade
gamepad.description: Modes for regular controllers, dance pads and arcade games.
features: BEMANI: Pop'n Music, Beatmania IIDX and GuitarFreaks
Arcade I/O for PDLoader and Spice2x

wiiBluetooth.title: Wii & Wii U: Wii Remote emulation
wiiBluetooth.subtitle: Connects over Bluetooth. No console mods or homebrew needed.
wiiBluetooth.alertBody: Santroller can act as a Wii Remote over Bluetooth, so you can play Guitar Hero, Band Hero and DJ Hero on a stock Wii or Wii U with retail discs.
wiiBluetooth.hardwarePicoW: Raspberry Pi Pico W / Pico 2 W: uses the built-in CYW43439 Bluetooth radio.
wiiBluetooth.hardwarePicoWWarning: Some cheap "Pico W" boards from AliExpress use an ESP8285/ESP8266 chip instead. These don't have Bluetooth and won't work.
wiiBluetooth.hardwareDongle: Regular Pico + Bluetooth dongle: plug a CSR8510 or BCM20702 dongle into the Pico's USB host port.
pairingSteps: Turn on Wii Remote Emulation for your device in the Configurator.
Turn on your instrument and the Wii / Wii U.
Press the SYNC button on the console, then press SYNC on your controller.
The controller connects as a Wii Remote with a guitar or drum extension.

brainslug.title: Wii: Santroller Brainslug
brainslug.subtitle: Lets Guitar Hero, Band Hero and DJ Hero on Wii use wired USB instruments
brainslug.intro: Guitar Hero and DJ Hero on Wii only look for instruments plugged into a Wii Remote. If you're using a wired USB controller without Bluetooth, Santroller Brainslug is a homebrew patch that makes these games read USB instruments instead.
discSteps: Extract sd.zip to the root of your Wii's SD card.
Plug your instrument into one of the Wii's USB ports.
Insert the game disc and open the Homebrew Channel.
Launch Brainslug. The game will boot with USB instrument support.
brainslug.usbLoaderAlertTitle: Load games from USB, not SD
brainslug.usbLoaderAlertBody: The game has to be loaded from a USB drive. Loading it from the SD card stops Brainslug from loading its modules.
usbLoaderSteps: Extract sd.zip to the root of your SD card.
In /bcs/dols/, rename RGHE52.dol to the Title ID of your game (e.g. SXEE52.dol for Guitar Hero 5). Make a copy for each game you want to use.
Select the game and go to Settings → Game Load.
Set Custom Game IOS to 249 (or your cIOS slot).
Save, plug in your instrument and start the game.

pademu.title: PS2: PADEMU in Open PS2 Loader
pademu.subtitle: Use USB instruments in older PS2 games on a modded PS2
pademu.intro: Older PS2 games, including Guitar Hero 1 and 2, only read controllers in the front controller ports and ignore USB. PADEMU, built into Open PS2 Loader, makes USB controllers show up as PS2 controllers.
pademu.note: Note: Santroller switches to PS3 mode when plugged into a PS2. PADEMU sees a PS3 guitar and presents it to the game as a PS2 Guitar Hero controller. PADEMU only works for games launched from OPL, not retail discs.
steps: Plug your Santroller controller into one of the PS2's USB ports.
Plug a normal PS2 controller into port 2, so you can still get around the menus.
Make sure you have a recent build of <extlink>Open PS2 Loader (OPL) <icon /></extlink>.
Start OPL and press Start to open Settings.
Set Settings For Port to 1P and Emulation to On.

orbis.title: PS4: OrbisInstrumentalizer
orbis.subtitle: Removes instrument restrictions on a jailbroken PS4
orbis.cardSubtitle: A GoldHEN plugin for jailbroken PS4s.
orbis.cardBody: Patches Rock Band 4 and Guitar Hero Live to remove the instrument and authentication checks, so any USB guitar or drum kit works without an auth controller plugged into the USB Host port.

auth.alertBody: The Xbox One, Xbox Series, PS4 and PS5 regularly ask controllers to prove they're official. A controller that can't answer gets disconnected after about 8 minutes.

builtIn.title: 1. Built in
builtIn.body: Santroller handles Xbox 360 authentication itself. No extra hardware needed.

usbPassthrough.title: 2. USB passthrough
usbPassthrough.body: Plug an official controller, most third-party Xbox One controllers, or an auth dongle into the USB Host port. Santroller passes the console's requests through to it.

harvestedChip.title: 3. Auth chip (I2C)
harvestedChip.body: Take the auth chip off an Xbox One controller board and wire it to the Pico over I2C. This handles Xbox One / Series authentication without anything plugged in.

noAuth.title: 4. Avoid it
noAuth.body:
Some setups don't need authentication at all:
• Fortnite Festival: Keyboard profiles
• Rock Band 4 on PS4/PS5: PS3 instrument mode

auth.hardwareSubtitle: With one of these on the USB Host port, or an auth chip wired over I2C, Santroller answers the console's auth requests automatically:

xbone.hardware: Official or most third-party wired Xbox One / Series controllers, or an Xbox One auth chip (I2C)
xbone.notes: Most third-party Xbox One controllers work over USB Host. You can also wire an auth chip from an Xbox One controller to the Pico's I2C pins so nothing needs to be plugged in.

ps4.hardware: DualShock 4 or Mayflash MAGPS4 / Magicboots PS4 dongle
ps4.notes: Leave the dongle or controller plugged in while you play.

ps5.notes: Needed for PS5 games. Magicboots PS4/S5 don't work with PS5 games.

festival.alertBody: There's no dedicated Fortnite Festival mode. Instead you create a profile, which lets you choose your own key bindings, pick keyboard or controller output, and play on consoles without an auth dongle.

keyboard.title: Keyboard profiles on consoles
keyboard.subtitle: No auth dongle needed
keyboard.body1: PS4, PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series consoles require controllers to authenticate, and will disconnect a controller that can't after about 8 minutes.
keyboard.body2: Keyboards don't need to authenticate, and Fortnite Festival supports keyboard controls. If you set up a Keyboard profile, your guitar or drums show up as a USB keyboard and you can play without any extra hardware.
keyboard.badge: Works on PS4, PS5, Xbox One & Series

pc.title: Playing on PC
pc.subtitle: Controller or keyboard
pc.body: On PC, Fortnite Festival works with both guitar controllers and keyboards:
options: Guitar: Use a Guitar Hero or Rock Band profile with XInput. Turn on Send Select as D-pad Left in the profile options so Overdrive works.
Keyboard: Use a Keyboard profile if you'd rather bind your own keys.

steps.title: Setting up a Fortnite Festival profile
steps.addProfile: Add a profile: Under Profiles in the sidebar, click Add profile and give it a name like Fortnite Keyboard.
steps.setEmulation: Switch it to keyboard: In the profile options, set Device to Emulate to Keyboard / Mouse.
steps.loadPreset: Load a preset (optional): Under Mappings, pick one of the Presets:
presets: Fortnite Festival - Guitar (Lead): frets on D, F, J, K, L and Overdrive on Space.
Fortnite Festival - Pro Guitar: frets on 1-5, strum on Right Shift / Right Ctrl, whammy on Slash and tilt on PageDown.
Fortnite Festival - Drums / Pro Drums: pads and cymbals on the default drum keys.
steps.customize: Change bindings: Click any input to bind it to a different key. Just make sure it matches your Fortnite settings.
steps.navigation: Menu navigation: Bind keys like the arrow keys, Enter and Escape to buttons or button combos (e.g. Start + Select) so you can get around Fortnite's menus.
steps.assignments: Choose when it's used: Under Assignments, set the profile as the default, or have it activate when you hold a button (like Green or Start) while plugging in.
